html:
A great earthquake that struck the industrial city of Tangshan, about 150 km east of Beijing, early on 28 July 1976. It hit at night, while people slept, and destroyed most of the city's buildings in seconds.

The official death toll is about 242,000; some estimates are far higher. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes of the twentieth century.

It came in a year of turmoil. Zhou Enlai had died in January, and the Cultural Revolution was near its end. The government refused foreign aid and gave the toll only years later. In Chinese tradition, great disasters were read as a sign that a ruler had lost the Mandate of Heaven, and many saw the quake that way when Mao Zedong died six weeks later.

Tangshan was rebuilt as a new city. Compare the Shaanxi earthquake of 1556, the deadliest on record, and the Sichuan earthquake of 2008.
